topics.label: Río Andarax restoration works (2023 procurement)
topics.description: A proposed hydrological and ecological restoration works contract for the Río Andarax, covering Alhabia, Santa Fe de Mondújar, Gádor, Rioja and Benahadux. The June 2023 justification combines flood-risk reduction for neighbouring agricultural land with recovery of native river habitats and natural/ethnographic heritage. Measures include restoring conveyance, native vegetation and traditional balates, transverse structures and boqueras, with interpretive access. The document gives an 18-month execution period, a 106.5 ha project scope and a tender budget of EUR 3,416,081.25 including VAT. The October document evaluates bidders’ technical submissions; neither source certifies completed works or ecological outcomes. Measured restoration outcomes and long-term performance are not reported in the reviewed material.

topics.label: Almería and Campo de Níjar fluvial restoration
topics.description: A formally assigned restoration works project for 56 ramblas in three sectors: Almería, Campo de Níjar–Artal and Cabo de Gata. The December 2022 assignment to TRAGSA combines removal of agro-waste/construction debris and invasive exotic vegetation, conveyance improvements and bank defence with native riparian planting of certified provenance. It also provides for an interpreted public river path on lower Rambla Morales in the Cabo de Gata–Níjar protected area. The maximum assigned budget is EUR 3,866,930.52, with an initial 24-month period and PRTR C4.I3 financing. These records establish an assignment and delivery obligations, not completed hectares or measured ecological recovery. Separate 2023 supervision and 2024 plant-supply documents retain their own roles and dates. Measured restoration outcomes and long-term performance are not reported in the reviewed material.

topics.label: Níjar works supervision and environmental surveillance
topics.description: The June 2023 TRAGSATEC assignment separately covers assistance to works direction, health/safety coordination and environmental surveillance for the Almería/Campo de Níjar project. Surveillance must check implementation and effectiveness of protective/corrective measures, investigate unsatisfactory performance, detect unanticipated impacts and report to works direction and the environmental authority. The assignment budget is EUR 151,606.30. Its initial 24-month period starts with the works and can extend through completion and required documentation. Monthly certification and PRTR milestone reports are delivery controls; this document does not provide the monitoring results. Its inconsistent subcontracting statements remain unresolved. This remains a delivery activity within the restoration project, rather than an independent ecological trial.

topics.label: Campo de Níjar native plant supply roster
topics.description: The 8 August 2024 TSA0078436 specification requests plants for planting and replacement of failures in the semi-arid fluvial-restoration works. Two lots list 22 named taxa in 23 supply rows, including two container sizes for Populus alba. Carob appears as 1,376 units in 1 L nursery containers; jujube as 9,407 units in 1 L containers. These are requested supply quantities and nursery stock volumes, not confirmed installed plants, an ecological association, reservoir capacity or irrigation doses. Lot 2 is expressly described as native species of the Levante Almeriense. The contract imposes provenance, plant health, root architecture and delivery acceptance requirements. Source spellings and uncertain taxonomy remain visible; no working community or plant count is changed. This remains a delivery activity within the restoration project, rather than an independent ecological trial.
